events.title: Marcus Aurelius becomes Roman Emperor
events.description: On the death of Antoninus Pius, Marcus Aurelius succeeded and made his adoptive brother Lucius Verus co-emperor. A Stoic philosopher, he wrote his 'Meditations' while campaigning on the Danube.
events.html: On the death of Antoninus Pius, Marcus Aurelius succeeded and made his adoptive brother Lucius Verus co-emperor. A Stoic philosopher, he wrote his 'Meditations' while campaigning on the Danube.

events.title: Napoleon storms Jaffa
events.description: French troops took the port of Jaffa during Napoleon's Syrian campaign. Thousands of prisoners were then executed, and plague broke out in the army, which was halted at Acre.
events.html: French troops took the port of Jaffa during Napoleon's Syrian campaign. Thousands of prisoners were then executed, and plague broke out in the army, which was halted at Acre.

events.title: Daniel Webster's 'Seventh of March' speech backs compromise
events.description: The Massachusetts senator supported Henry Clay's compromise proposals, including a tougher fugitive slave law, to preserve the Union. Many Northern abolitionists denounced him.
events.html: The Massachusetts senator supported Henry Clay's compromise proposals, including a tougher fugitive slave law, to preserve the Union. Many Northern abolitionists denounced him.

events.title: Alexander Graham Bell is granted his telephone patent
events.description: US Patent 174,465 covered a method of transmitting speech electrically. It became one of the most valuable patents ever issued and was defended in hundreds of lawsuits.
events.html: US Patent 174,465 covered a method of transmitting speech electrically. It became one of the most valuable patents ever issued and was defended in hundreds of lawsuits.

events.title: German troops reoccupy the Rhineland
events.description: Hitler sent soldiers into the demilitarised Rhineland in breach of the Versailles and Locarno treaties. France and Britain did not respond with force, encouraging further German expansion.
events.html: Hitler sent soldiers into the demilitarised Rhineland in breach of the Versailles and Locarno treaties. France and Britain did not respond with force, encouraging further German expansion.

events.title: US troops seize the Remagen bridge over the Rhine
events.description: American soldiers captured the Ludendorff railway bridge at Remagen before German demolition charges could destroy it. It gave the Allies their first crossing of the Rhine.
events.html: American soldiers captured the Ludendorff railway bridge at Remagen before German demolition charges could destroy it. It gave the Allies their first crossing of the Rhine.

events.title: 'Bloody Sunday' on the Edmund Pettus Bridge in Selma
events.description: Alabama state troopers attacked about 600 civil rights marchers with clubs and tear gas. Televised images shocked the nation and helped secure the Voting Rights Act that August.
events.html: Alabama state troopers attacked about 600 civil rights marchers with clubs and tear gas. Televised images shocked the nation and helped secure the Voting Rights Act that August.
